overview: Against the McDonnell Attack 2.f4, Black strikes in the centre with 2...e5, a reversed King's Gambit Declined with Black already committed to ...c5. White usually plays 3.Nf3 and fxe5 or Bc4, developing normally and exploiting the loosened Black queenside. Black gets space and a solid centre, but the line is rare.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nf3, Bc4 and castle, hitting the e5 pawn with fxe5
Use the f-file and attack on f7
Play Nc3 and d3 for a solid set-up

black_ideas.idea: Capture on f4 and use ...d5 to break
Keep the pawn structure and play ...d6

typical_structures.structure: Centre with White e4/f4 against Black c5/e5 pawns
Black can take on f4 for an open f-file

character.notes: Black has a solid centre and White a normal development, with tactics on f4 and e5.

gambit.notes: No pawn is given up in the typical line; Black can exchange on f4 and White regains it.

soundness.notes: Black's centre play is a reasonable answer to 2.f4.

structure.notes: Pawn tension on e5 and f4 stays undecided for some moves.

approach.notes: The Mafia move is a rare reply that strong players seldom pick.

level.notes: Pawn structure and tactics around f4 need care, with little theory.
